text:
Good name in man and woman, dear my lord,
Is the immediate jewel of their souls.
Who steals my purse steals trash. ’Tis something, nothing;
’Twas mine, ’tis his, and has been slave to thousands.
But he that filches from me my good name
Robs me of that which not enriches him
And makes me poor indeed.
plain: Your name is the one thing you own that can't be replaced. Steal your cash and you took nothing. Steal your name and you took everything.
Jealousy feeds on itself. It makes the pain it claims to be reacting to.
Enough is a kind of wealth. No amount is enough if you live afraid of losing it.
Don't act on suspicion. See it, test it, prove it, then decide.

text:
I swear ’tis better to be much abus’d
Than but to know’t a little.
plain: Knowing a little is worse than knowing nothing or knowing all. Half-information is torture.

text:
He that is robb’d, not wanting what is stol’n,
Let him not know’t, and he’s not robb’d at all.
plain: What you never knew about can't hurt you. Pain often lives in the knowing, not the event.

text:
Farewell the tranquil mind! Farewell content!
Farewell the plumed troops and the big wars
That make ambition virtue!
plain: Once peace of mind goes, ambition and glory mean nothing. Guard your calm first.

text:
Excellent wretch! Perdition catch my soul,
But I do love thee! And when I love thee not,
Chaos is come again.
plain: Love is what holds the world together for him. Take it away and everything turns back to chaos.

text:
Men should be what they seem;
Or those that be not, would they might seem none!
plain: Be what you seem, or stop seeming. People who fake it are the ones who rot first.

text:
I should be wise; for honesty’s a fool,
And loses that it works for.
plain: The cynic's creed: honesty costs you and pays nothing. Notice when you start believing it.

text: Nay, that’s certain. But yet the pity of it, Iago! O Iago, the pity of it, Iago!
plain: Seeing the waste of what could have been good is the real grief.

text: No, my heart is turned to stone; I strike it, and it hurts my hand. O, the world hath not a sweeter creature. She might lie by an emperor’s side, and command him tasks.
plain: You can try to harden yourself, but the feeling is still there, and it hurts you, not them.

text:
Had it pleas’d heaven
To try me with affliction, had they rain’d
All kinds of sores and shames on my bare head,
Steep’d me in poverty to the very lips,
Given to captivity me and my utmost hopes,
I should have found in some place of my soul
A drop of patience.
plain: He could take poverty, scorn and captivity. What broke him was losing the thing his heart was built on.

text:
It makes us, or it mars us, think on that,
And fix most firm thy resolution.
plain: Big moments make you or break you. Think on that, then commit fully.

text:
He hath a daily beauty in his life
That makes me ugly.
plain: Envy in one line: someone else's good life makes you feel ugly.
Ask to be remembered as you were, no excuses and no smear. Own it, and know that love can outrun judgment.

text: Who can control his fate? ’Tis not so now.
plain: Nobody controls their fate, however strong they once were.

text:
Here is my journey’s end, here is my butt,
And very sea-mark of my utmost sail.
plain: Every road has an end and every sail has a limit. Know where yours is.

text:
Thou hast not half that power to do me harm
As I have to be hurt. O gull! O dolt!
plain: You can't scare someone who has nothing left to lose. Truth makes people dangerous to power.

text:
’Tis not a year or two shows us a man:
They are all but stomachs and we all but food;
They eat us hungerly, and when they are full,
They belch us.
plain: It takes more than a year or two to know a person. Appetite and love can look the same early on.

text:
For death remember’d should be like a mirror,
Who tells us life’s but breath, to trust it error.
plain: Remember you will die and you stop trusting that life is permanent. It's just breath.

text:
Then it is thus: the passions of the mind,
That have their first conception by misdread,
Have after-nourishment and life by care;
And what was first but fear what might be done,
Grows elder now and cares it be not done.
plain: Fear starts as a guess about what might happen. Feed it with worry and it turns into something that runs your life.

text:
They do abuse the king that flatter him:
For flattery is the bellows blows up sin;
plain: Flatterers do you harm. Praise is fuel for the worst in you.

text:
I knew him tyrannous; and tyrants’ fears
Decrease not, but grow faster than the years:
plain: Tyrants never get safe. Their fear grows faster than their years.

text: Who makes the fairest show means most deceit.
plain: The sweeter the offer looks, the more you should check what it's hiding.

text:
One sorrow never comes but brings an heir,
That may succeed as his inheritor;
plain: Trouble rarely shows up alone. One bad thing brings the next.

text:
What need we fear?
The ground’s the lowest, and we are half way there.
plain: When you're already at the bottom, there's nothing left to fear. Only up from here.

text:
Opinion’s but a fool, that makes us scan
The outward habit by the inward man.
plain: Judging people by how they look is a fool's habit. Read what's inside.

text:
Whereby I see that time’s the king of men,
He’s both their parent, and he is their grave,
And gives them what he will, not what they crave.
plain: Time makes you and buries you. It hands out what it wants, not what you asked for.

text:
What I have been I have forgot to know;
But what I am, want teaches me to think on:
plain: Who you used to be is gone. Need teaches you to think about who you are now.

text:
Courage enough: I do not fear the flaw;
It hath done to me the worst.
plain: When the worst has already happened, the storm loses its power over you.

text:
I hold it ever,
Virtue and cunning were endowments greater
Than nobleness and riches: careless heirs
May the two latter darken and expend;
But immortality attends the former,
Making a man a god.
plain: Skill and virtue outlast money and rank. Heirs waste the rest, but what you learn stays.

text:
We cannot but obey
The powers above us. Could I rage and roar
As doth the sea she lies in, yet the end
Must be as ’tis.
plain: You can't rage the sea into calming. Some things end how they end, so spend the energy on what you can do.
If you're born to a position, act like it. If it was handed to you, earn the right to it.
